title: Which AI Tool to use for a Text-based Incremental Game
author: ansehelm
selftext: Good day people. I have some concept on a text-heavy incremental game that I wish to build a prototype for. Currently I'm using normal ChatGPT (Go) for brainstorming and discussion with the AI, then later I tried to do the brainstorming and discussion on Claude (Free), but every time it hits the 5-hour limit quickly, although it is thorough and provide some useful insight on mathematics and game mechanics. My question is, if I want to proceed further, which platform would you suggest me to put money into? I can see that ChatGPT (Codex) seems to have much higher limit compared to Claude, but Claude seems to provide better insight.

comments.author: Semantic_meaning
comments.body: I'll throw some free build credits your way to see if [https://pompeii.ai](https://pompeii.ai) could do that

comments.author: Fringe_Walker_
comments.body: I personally havn't used Claude, but I've used Chat GPT and Gemini and feel like im getting some decent progress made with my own 2 projects. Do mabye check out Gemini? I use the free versions of both.

comments.author: Fizassist1
comments.body:
For my project I use chatgpt to walk me through things and write scripts, but im doing most of the work by hand in Godot.  It actually has worked very well, and I've made 3 mini games for my educational game in the past week doing it this way.

I use gpt to generate assets, then touch up in asprite.  

I've used comfyui desktop too for some of my raw assets, if you have a desktop to run it.  

I've found success using ludo ai and pixel lab for the animation side of things.

I guess I use a lot of different ai tools for different purposes, but I still like having my complete control so I still do all the work in Godot.

comments.author: VR38DET
comments.body: Use claude or codex it doesn’t make much difference in fact i suggest you trial a month each to see which you like better based off your own experience.
